newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Howard takes 18-strong business group to China.
newsitem.headline: Howard takes 18-strong business group to China.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Wednesday that Lachlan Murdoch, the managing director of News Limited, the Australian arm of News Corp, would be among a 18-strong business delegation to accompany him on a trip to China this week.
"(It) is probably the most senior and most broadly representative business group to accompany an Australian prime minister on an overseas visit," Howard told parliament.
Howard's visit is intended to boost trade links.
The prime minister's office issued a statement listing these members of the business delegation:
- John Allen, president, Australia China Business Council.
- Tony Berg, managing director of Boral Ltd.
- Trevor Flugge, chairman of the Australian Wheat Board.
- Charles Goode, chairman of ANZ Banking Group Ltd.
- Geoff Kells, managing director of CSR Ltd.
- Athol Lapthorne, chairman of Amcor Ltd.
- Simon Lee, chairman of the Western Australia Chinese Chamber of Commerce and of Equigold NL.
- Catherine Livingstone, managing director of Cochlear Ltd.
- Sir Russell Madigan, chairman of Australian United Steel Industry Ltd.
- Hugh Morgan, managing director of WMC Ltd.
- Alec Morrison, chairman of the International Wool Secretariat.
- David Mortimer, managing director and chief executive officer of TNT Ltd, a unit of Dutch group PTT Nederland NV.
- Lachlan Murdoch, executive director of News Corp.
- David Murray, managing director of Commonwealth Bank of Australia Ltd.
- Maurice Newman, chairman, Australian Stock Exchange.
- Peter Smedley, group managing director, Colonial Ltd.
- Lewis Ting, chief executive officer of Ernst and Young in Australia.
- Geoff Tomlinson, managing director, National Mutual Holdings Ltd
